comment: Professor Xu is a really great guy but I found the class confusing.He cares a lot about his students and is a generous grader (gives a lot of partial credit), so it is not difficult to pass if you are lost like I was.There is a short quiz about once a week so make sure you don't fall behind.Definitely take for credit if you can't get anyone else.

I enjoyed the lectures, and topics in class. Most of the questions on exams come directly from problems in the worksheets. Problems in the homework assignment are much more difficult than problems in exams preparing you for the tests. As long as you keep up with the in-class work and review it before tests, you should be fine.

Prof. Xu is new to Richmond. Other reviews are correct in saying that the first test was extremely difficult–it was, but Prof. Xu adjusted the grading structure to account for that. For MATH 235 he assigns pre-class videos but doesn't go beyond the videos too much during the lecture and then hands out often confusing worksheets.

The first test was very hard and had a D average, but after that the class improved for the other midterm and final. Class time was not efficient, and course material is learned from videos outside of class, but easy homework is worth a lot of the grade.

It was a great time in Calc 3! At first, it was a little unclear about the grading, but he was very flexible and adjusted the difficulty of exams after the first one. 25% of the grade is from doing online homework which is very nice in math class. The slides from the lectures are recorded and you can access them any time. Great experience!

This professor was strong at articulating complicated, technical topics in simple, easy to understand ways. Purely on his teaching I would give him a 5, but there was an inconsistent range of difficulty for tests. Two tests had a reasonable difficulty, but our first test was unreasonably hard. Still, a great professor for math interested people.

Dr. Xu's class is not clear at all; all the concepts he provides are ambiguous, and most of the time he did not prepare understandable examples. lf watching videos is a necessity for learning, then the significance of attending classes is just to supplement the videos. He didn't give clear scoring and grading standards.
